notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: By headlines of 28 November, US forces disabled a commercial ship trying to leave Iran and Tehran vowed to confront the blockade, Reuters reported Washington urging Iraq and Venezuela to leave OPEC, Iraq restarted its pipeline to Turkey at 300,000 barrels a day and Lukoil agreed to sell its foreign assets. After the BBC and RNZ reported the UN climate talks' collapse and Handelsblatt a week of global temperature above two degrees, Australia's parliament passed a scheme reserving gas for its home market and Colombia's tax law was forecast to raise electric car prices by 14%. Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 12,000 cases amid fighting in Ituri, the US and Mexico are reported losing measles elimination and Gaza's doctors warn of a meningitis wave. Hackers were reported inside a US Air Force cloud service, a study confirmed that a Russian satellite deliberately approached a radar satellite of the Finnish firm Iceye, and Poland signed a $300 million contract with Palantir. From earlier days stand the reported Iranian drone deaths of two Italians in Kuwait, which Iran denies, the Turkish ruling that ended Ekrem İmamoğlu's presidential bid, the Cairo tanker fire that killed 31, and Jensen Huang's hearing due on 1 December after reports of Trump's Nvidia trades.
moved: The blockades thread turned on 28 November: its continuation read the US disabling a ship leaving Iran beside reported US pressure on Iraq and Venezuela to leave OPEC, Iraq's pipeline restart and Lukoil's sale as Washington deciding who sells oil, and dropped Gaza and the Baltic, so the reason for keeping it apart from the Iran thread was withdrawn.

A 3 November expectation from the Iran war thread was kept on 28 November, when Ammon reported Iraq resuming its oil pipeline to Turkey at 300,000 barrels a day, a route that avoids Hormuz; the line's own history of disputes between Baghdad, Erbil and Ankara means it says less about Hormuz than it seems.

The 10 November narrative on gas sought in the hottest years, never given a thread, was resumed after fifteen editions as governments securing their own fuel after the climate talks failed; a thread on old diseases returning was built from the notebook; and the spying thread was revived after two editions as militaries renting clouds and satellites.

Three expectations failed on 28 November with nothing reported: the FAA naming one fault for its 13 November ground stop, a Russian or Iranian official citing a named strike to delay talks, and a turbine, transformer or battery maker reporting a record backlog tied to the Gulf war, set by a 6 November narrative the Chronicle never gave a thread.
silent: The Iran war thread has had no narrative since 24 November; on 27 and 28 November its events, the Kuwait deaths and the ship disabled leaving Iran, came in the blockades thread, and its own 3 November expectation was kept on 28 November, so the silence is the editions' division, not the war going quiet.

The thread on middle powers' trade deals has had no narrative on 26, 27 or 28 November, and no new report of the US tariff list has come in any narrative since 25 November; that may be the sample as much as the world.

The thread on civilian places readied for drone strikes has had no narrative since 25 November; the Houthi strike on Jazan came in the blockades thread on 27 November, so its subject is still reported in part.
The thread on health payments drawn into state channels still rests on one narrative from 24 November, with nothing since on Kenya's paybill order or Jordan's cash ban.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, talks and reach
threads.text: From 26 October it followed the Gulf talks and the Hormuz price shock to jet fuel, mortgages, wages and rates; the war was reported paused on 8 November. From 13 to 21 November strikes on Bahrain and Qeshm, tankers hit off Hormuz and a downed US drone came in other threads, and four of its price expectations failed. Revived by judgment on 24 November: US petrol fell 66 cents in a month and Qatar's emir mediated. On 27 November Iranian drones were reported killing two Italian technicians in Kuwait, which Iran denies, and on 28 November US forces disabled a commercial ship leaving Iran; both came in the blockades thread. On 28 November its 3 November expectation of a Gulf export route avoiding Hormuz was kept, as Ammon reported Iraq resuming its pipeline to Turkey at 300,000 barrels a day. No narrative has carried it since 24 November.
threads.direction: After a pause was reported on 24 November, by 28 November attacks around the Gulf and a US naval blockade of Iran were reported again, carried in the blockades thread.

threads.label: Governments setting pump prices mid-war
threads.text: Begun on 7 November: Italy would not extend its diesel excise cut, Portugal adjusted its fuel tax discount and Taiwan's CPC held pump prices after absorbing NT$34.07 billion, joined as governments handing the war's fuel price back to drivers. After four editions without a narrative the Chronicle revived it on 12 November with an unlinked narrative marked firm: Pakistan cut petrol and diesel prices, Chile resubmitted a bill freezing fuel prices until February, Greece set €32 million for islanders' sea transport and Indonesian ferry operators asked to raise fares, with crude below $90. Its case against says the decisions move in different directions and none names Hormuz. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to early December.
threads.direction: It has moved from governments ending fuel tax cuts to governments keeping pump prices in their own hands and paying the gap from budgets as crude fell below $90.

threads.label: Shared systems failing, from outages to patches
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand, it ran through AI-led US growth, Taiwan's state buyers, borrowing and the Nvidia case to 12 November, then followed shared systems stopping: a Microsoft outage at British councils and Australia's federal police, the FAA's nationwide halt, the fallback left to households and faults hard to tell from attacks. On 18 November South Korea's Digital Daily blamed patches for AI-found flaws for failures at the NSA, in finance and in aviation. No narrative has carried it since. Three of its early market expectations failed between 22 and 25 November, while the Nasdaq's fall from historic highs on 25 November kept one. On 28 November its expectation that the FAA would name one fault for the 13 November ground stop failed, with nothing reported.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and borrowing to public services stopping when one system fails, to who holds the backup, to telling a fault from an attack, and by 18 November to patches for AI-found flaws named as a cause.

threads.label: AI labs financed by suppliers, then public shareholders
threads.text: Begun on 10 November, when TSMC was reported investing NT$32 billion in OpenAI and Anthropic. Its expectation that Anthropic would cut or delay its listing failed on 17 November. On 18 November Anthropic priced at $83 a share as the ECB compared the AI build to subprime, and on 19 November it passed $3 trillion on its first day. It was resumed on 22 November, marked tentative: Anthropic lost 147 trillion won of market value in one day, Kommersant tied bitcoin's two-year low to the share offering, Musk warned of an AI funding shortage next year and Oracle said it has the funds for its OpenAI contract. Its case against says the 21 November reading of high rates fits the same headlines. No narrative carried it on 24, 25 or 26 November, so it is silent; on 26 November Anthropic's further fall came in the revived thread on public money for AI.
threads.direction: It has moved from chip suppliers funding the AI labs, to the labs selling shares to the public at record prices, to the listing's own fall and the claim that its size draws money from other risky assets.

threads.label: Soldiers sent against disorder, gangs and smugglers
threads.text: Begun on 5 November, marked tentative: Indonesia's troops in Jakarta, Pakistan's army for Punjab by-elections, a Bangladeshi soldier killed raiding traffickers at Teknaf and a French bill widening when police may fire. After eleven editions without a narrative it was resumed on 19 November as crime fought as war: Haiti's forces fought gangs with Salvadoran troops in the country, Colombia's president counted a tenth bombing and weighed asking Congress for US troops, fishermen sued Washington over a drone strike at sea and the OAS called a session on organised crime. On 20 November France's parliament definitively adopted the law presuming police use of weapons lawful, keeping the 5 November expectation, in the youth protest thread. Its case against says the military role in each is decades old. No narrative carried it on 20, 21 or 22 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from soldiers keeping order on home streets to armies, aircraft and foreign troops fighting gangs and smugglers, with results counted as deaths and strikes.

threads.label: Seats, borders and talks used as pressure
threads.text: Begun on 11 November and marked tentative: the CSTO stripped Armenia of its vote, Turkey excluded Israel from COP31 in Antalya, and Washington and Moscow asked Europe to choose one negotiator for the Ukraine talks. On 12 November it was carried on as entry of every kind: Israel will bar Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Washington's envoys said Europeans would join the next round, and Putin spoke of US visas for Russian Olympians. On 13 November the single-negotiator expectation failed when the EU agreed a team of five countries and EU institutions, which weakens the reading of entry as a bargaining move. Its ground passed on 14 November to the thread on Europe's security bargained elsewhere. No narrative has carried it since 12 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It moved from seats in alliances and summits to entry of every kind, and on 13 November Europe was admitted to the Ukraine talks on its own terms, against the thread's reading.

threads.label: Leaders' children judged on their own conduct
threads.text: Begun on 12 November and marked tentative by its own edition. Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice-president over a certificate scandal, Sara Duterte's impeachment trial is to resume after the ASEAN summit, Donald Trump Jr left an adviser's role at Kalshi over a conflict with a rival investment, and Nigeria's president congratulated his son Seyi on a traditional title. The join is what a leader's name entitles a child to hold. Its case against says the cases share a family tie and little else. On 18 November its expectation was kept, loosely, when R7 reported Brazil's prosecutor-general filing a criminal complaint against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. On 27 November a new thread on degrees and records deciding candidacy began; Gibran's certificate scandal is the nearest event to it, and Indonesia's choice of his successor appears there.

threads.label: Nvidia case: trade controls and the president's favour
threads.text: Begun on 13 November, marked firm, as Bessent blamed Lutnick for Megaspeed not being blacklisted. On 17 November Washington proposed extending chip controls to Southeast Asia. On 24 November the board reinstated Huang with Trump claiming the deal, and Megaspeed was blacklisted. On 25 November it widened to favour, as the attorney general called Nvidia a good corporate citizen during the investigation. On 26 November, marked plausible, the BBC reported Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, Observador that he would pardon Huang 'if necessary', and Democrats opened an inquiry into his lobbying, while Huawei rejected its US conviction; the join became exposure to US trade law by nationality and closeness. Its case against says Nvidia has not been charged and the pardon remark is conditional. No narrative carried it on 27 or 28 November; Huang's hearing is due on 1 December.
threads.direction: It has moved from a dispute between US departments over chips reaching China, to penalties on firms abroad, to the firm's treatment set beside its chief's closeness to the president, and by 26 November to the president's own trades and an offered pardon.

threads.label: Long-range strikes during Russia and Iran talks
threads.text: Begun on 13 November, marked plausible: as the EU named its team for the Ukraine talks, a Ukrainian drone hit a Russian warship, bombs went off in Moscow and Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain. Resumed on 17 November, marked tentative, with crossings as targets: the Crimean Bridge twice, Kyiv's bridges, a rail line to Hungary and Iran's Qeshm Island. On 19 November Lenta reported Trump saying Putin is angry at Zelensky over the Crimean Bridge attack, keeping the 17 November expectation, and on 26 November von der Leyen was reported proposing an energy ceasefire, keeping a 13 November one. On 28 November its other 13 November expectation, that a Russian or Iranian official would cite a named strike as a reason to delay talks or harden terms, failed with nothing reported. No narrative has carried it since 17 November.
threads.direction: It has moved from strikes on bases, ships and oil sites far from the fronts to strikes on bridges and islands in the days before the three-power meeting, and by 26 November to a proposal to halt strikes on energy sites.

threads.label: Frontiers, ships and host states after the declaration
threads.text: Begun on 14 November, when Zelensky said Washington floated Ukraine giving up Donbas for NATO membership. On 20 November Estonia set 1 December to close its Russian crossings; on 22 November a Russian warship was sunk at Benghazi and Polish prosecutors said Russian cruise missiles fell in Poland. On 24 November Libya said it will sue Ukraine at the International Court of Justice and Finland had the damaged Sparta II towed out of its zone. Both its 14 November expectations failed, the second on 26 November, when Lenta also reported Finland's Stubb calling Putin, keeping a 19 November expectation the Chronicle had set aside on 20 November. On 27 November Russia and Poland's argument over a Baltic blockade came in the new thread on blockades. No narrative carried this one on 25, 26 or 27 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from allies fortifying and attacks on ships to countries where attacks land answering by naming the weapon, lawsuits, tows and radar aircraft, and its opening reading of a bargain over Europe's head is no longer held.

threads.label: Incomes set by rule falling behind prices
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. France had a fifth Saturday of protests against the cost of living and French police demanded a higher risk allowance; an Italian simulation put a 2028 pension more than 13,000 euros a year below one of twenty years earlier; a former Argentine judge warned of delays in retirees' claims, and a Canadian disability charity closed. The join is incomes fixed by law, decree or grant falling behind prices; its case against says the events share no cause. On 17 November a new thread on Europe's weekly protests took in the same French protest rounds. No narrative has carried it since 14 November, so it is silent; on 22 November pension policy through personal accounts began a thread of its own.

threads.label: Governments taking back roles in food supply
threads.text: Begun on 14 November with a narrative marked tentative that continues nothing. Nieuws.nl reports a fertiliser shortage caused by the Hormuz blockade threatening Dutch food security, Marib's farmers in Yemen have harvests and no open markets, Senegal calls rice a pillar of food sovereignty, New York is spending $70 million on five city-run grocery stores, Egypt's prime minister inspects a permanent state food fair, and Fortune reports nearby shops losing sales when Walmart leaves a town. The join is public authorities taking back choosing what is grown, securing inputs and selling food. Its case against says only the fertiliser story is new, Egypt's outlets date from the 1940s and New York's stores were a 2025 election promise. No narrative carried it on 17, 18 or 19 November, so it is silent; its expectations run to 5 and 12 December.

threads.label: Europe's protests over prices, met by top-ups
threads.text: Begun on 17 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts two weeks of protest over living costs and housing: 270,000 marched outside Paris on 6 November, Porto's housing camp put up tents on 8 November, Spain held its first general strike in 14 years on 11 November, and France counted 146,000 at a new round on 17 November. France brought forward a minimum wage rise and Italy's coalition argued over 300 euros for pensioners. Its case against says Spanish rents and French wages have different causes. No narrative has carried it since 17 November, so it is silent; on 20 November Gen Z marches across Europe and Bologna's general strike day came in the thread on young protesters.

threads.label: Defence decided by numbers of drones and interceptors
threads.text: Begun on 30 October with a narrative the Chronicle had not given a thread: cheap drones had made defence a matter of quantity again, so states were financing arms factories and widening conscription. After seventeen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 18 November, marked plausible, from the defending side: an Egyptian military expert told Al-Watan that closing the gap in US Patriot production will take years, the Jerusalem Post reported a rayon shortage threatening that production, Iran struck US assets in Kuwait, Bahrain and a UAE tanker, and a coalition struck the Houthis. Its case against says the Patriot shortfall has been discussed since 2023. No narrative has carried it since 18 November, so it is silent; on 25 November drone range came in a new thread on civilian places readied for strikes.
threads.direction: It has moved from cheap drones driving arms production and conscription to interceptor stocks that factories cannot refill quickly.

threads.label: Middle powers' trade deals as US tariffs loom
threads.text: Begun on 18 November, marked plausible, as Trump, Xi and Putin were reported meeting in China: EU governments approved signing their Indonesia agreement, Carney bet on Asia-Pacific trade and Vietnam, Chile, Peru and Egypt pressed their own deals, read as governments not waiting on the meeting. After five editions without a narrative it was resumed on 25 November, marked plausible and built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for a week: the EU and Indonesia signed on 21 November, India held talks with Canada and Belarus, Iraq and Egypt dropped entry visas, Jordan signed with Uzbekistan and Qatar talked trade with Canada, while outlets in Italy, Israel and Qatar reported Trump readying tariffs on China, Europe and fourteen more countries. Its case against says the deals predate any tariff list. No narrative carried it on 26, 27 or 28 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from deals made beside a three-power meeting to deals read as the answer to US tariffs, though no government is reported naming the tariffs as its reason.

threads.label: Strikes outside Europe over pay already owed
threads.text: Begun on 19 November with a narrative marked tentative, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative. It counts strikes and protests outside Europe since 5 November in Nigeria, Egypt, Bangladesh, Canada, Chile, Mexico and South Korea: on 19 November Nigeria's lecturers demanded withheld salaries, Zamalek's players complained of late dues, Bangladeshi garment workers clashed with police and Niagara's paramedics neared a strike, while the World Bank said Bangladesh is short of revenue. The join is pay already earned or promised and not paid, often by a state short of money. Its case against says the sample leans on three Nigerian papers. No narrative has carried it since 19 November; on 24 November Kashmir doctors' strike over stipends came in the new health payments thread.

threads.label: States offering money and sites to AI as shares fall
threads.text: Begun on 20 November, marked plausible and built from the site's notebook, so the story is older than its first narrative: Trump threatened to tax or sanction US firms building data centres abroad, Lagarde said EU funds should take first losses on chip plants and data centres, and CoreWeave fell below its listing price. After four editions without a narrative it was resumed on 26 November, marked tentative: the Dow swung more than 1,000 points on AI fears before recovering, Anthropic fell further and SuperX lost 18%, while Malaysia is exploring an AI wealth fund for citizens, the EU set out €50 billion for AI and quantum computing and the US approved Musk's plan for a million satellites hosting data centres. Its case against says the plans predate the sell-off and no government is buying the shares being sold. No narrative carried it on 27 or 28 November.
threads.direction: It has moved from states offering to site and underwrite data centres to governments committing funds and licences to AI while private holders sell, with the shift of risk to taxpayers an inference.

threads.label: Young protesters met by police and courts
threads.text: Begun on 31 October with protests called for the same weekend in several European countries, met with bans in some cities and talks in others; on 1 November its edition read them as governments meeting young protesters mainly with police numbers. After seventeen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 20 November, marked plausible and built from the site's notebook: pupils in Schleswig-Holstein struck against conscription, DW reported Gen Z protests in hundreds of European cities, keeping a 31 October expectation, a Lormont pupil went before the courts and France adopted its police weapons law. On 22 November the 1 November expectation of a German ban on a Gen Z protest citing violence in France failed, with nothing reported, as its own case against allowed. No narrative carried it on 21, 22 or 24 November, so it is silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from police numbers set against young protesters to courts, arrests and suspensions, and in Germany to a plan for military service.

threads.label: Breaches of records people are required to give
threads.text: Begun on 21 November, marked firm and built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for four days, so the story is older than its first narrative: attackers reached Transport for London's photocard records, the European Commission, the FBI's crime database and the US Agriculture Department, joined as records people must give the state. After three editions without a narrative it was resumed on 26 November, marked plausible: Bithumb says hackers sat unseen for more than two weeks and took resident registration numbers and transaction records, FinCEN is investigating unauthorised access and extended filing deadlines, and a hacker reached 1Password client data. The join moved to stores that anti-money-laundering rules require. Its case against says only two of six events fit. None of the 21 November breaches has been attributed in these headlines. No narrative carried it on 27 or 28 November; on 28 November 1Password's report came again in the spying thread.
threads.direction: It has moved from breaches of records the state requires to breaches of identity stores that anti-fraud rules oblige firms and regulators to keep.

threads.label: Gold, bitcoin and tech shares falling together
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. On 20 and 21 November the Nasdaq erased its gains for the year, gold fell more than $2,000 an ounce from its peak, bitcoin dropped below $55,000 for the first time since September 2024 and foreign investors pulled more than 3 trillion from Taiwan's market, as Trump attacked the Federal Reserve over rates. The join is the cost of borrowed money. On 22 November the AI financing thread read bitcoin's low as money drawn into AI listings, and on 24 November Al-Watan put gold's low down to US bond yields, this thread's reading. No narrative carried it on 22, 24 or 25 November, so it is silent; on 25 November the Economic Times reported the S&P 500 and Nasdaq falling back after historic highs, which sits poorly beside the 21 November report.

threads.label: Power projects placed on water already promised
threads.text: Begun on 21 November with a narrative marked tentative, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for five days, so the story is older than its first narrative. On 21 November Amit Shah backed India's Siang dam and promised dialogue with protesters, after a Sharavathi submergence report was promised to the Supreme Court and the court refused Tamil Nadu more Cauvery water. Taipei's mayoral campaign has fought over solar panels on the Feicui reservoir, Finland's largest conservation project failed when a utility would not sell the Palokki plant, and Bogotá warned on 18 November of water and power rationing under El Niño. The join is new hydro and solar placed on water already counted on. Its case against says half the evidence has nothing to do with power. No narrative carried it on 22, 24 or 25 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Consensus forums failing while courts and clubs decide
threads.text: Begun on 22 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. COP31 in Turkey ended without agreement after the EU rejected the final text, and UN talks on autonomous weapons ended without binding rules, while the International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya by nine votes to six and fifteen West African states adopted a migration declaration in Dakar. The join is that forums deciding by consensus failed while bodies that vote or admit only the willing decided. Its case against says climate talks collapsed at Copenhagen in 2009 and the contrast may be between judging and legislating. No narrative carried it on 24, 25 or 26 November, so it is silent; on 28 November the climate talks' collapse came in the revived thread on governments securing their own fuel.

threads.label: Pension policy run through personal accounts
threads.text: Begun on 22 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept since 17 November, so the story is older than its first narrative. On 17 November the US Treasury set rules for automatic retirement plans and Australia debated a superannuation shake-up; on 17 and 18 November Handelsblatt explained Germany's old-age provision deposit; on 20 November Singapore topped up the CPF accounts of more than 782,000 older citizens; on 22 November the Sydney Morning Herald argued for super for workers under 18 and RNZ said KiwiSaver fails the self-employed. The join is governments acting through individual accounts rather than the public pension, which Fortune reports is under six years from a 22% US cut. Its case against says these are adjustments to systems dating from 1955 to 2022. No narrative carried it on 24, 25 or 26 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Health payments drawn into state-run channels
threads.text: Begun on 24 November with a narrative marked tentative that continues nothing. Kenya's health ministry ordered public hospitals to stop taking payment through their own paybill numbers and the governors refused; Jordan's central bank banned cash payment of dues to medical providers; Himachal Pradesh handed its new health insurance scheme to the Aditya Birla Group. Public payers are slow: Rio Grande do Norte is late paying for orthopaedic surgeries, New Zealand's ACC refused a tradesman after decades of levies, and doctors in Jammu and Kashmir strike over stipends. The join is health money drawn into channels the state runs or chooses, and paid out slowly. Its case against says the motives differ, from county revenue to procurement, and the word payment may be doing the joining. No narrative carried it on 25, 26, 27 or 28 November, so it is silent.

threads.label: Civilian buildings and roads readied for drone strikes
threads.text: Begun on 25 November with a narrative marked plausible that continues nothing. Norway's NRK reports that hospitals now need bomb shelters, Iraq's defence minister ordered military units out of cities, French and Dutch jets practised landing on a Finnish motorway and Finland's hazard warning test went better. In the same days a Houthi attack hit the tallest tower in Riyadh's financial district for the second time in a week, a drone entered Polish airspace and Ukraine published another day's power cut schedules. The join is range: drones and missiles reach places far from any front, and governments prepare those places. Its case against says Finland has built shelters for decades and Iraq's order may concern Kurdish oilfields. No narrative carried it on 26, 27 or 28 November, so it is silent; on 27 November the Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery came in the blockades thread.

threads.label: States' spying and sabotage through private firms
threads.text: Begun on 25 November, marked tentative: NPR reported the US investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels, Finnish media suspected espionage at the Laukaa gunpowder factory and British firms supporting Ukraine were told to act against Russian sabotage. On 26 November French intelligence was reported naming Iran's Revolutionary Guard behind the supermarket hacking. Resumed on 28 November after two editions without a narrative, again tentative: outlets in Japan, the Netherlands and Israel report hackers inside a US Air Force cloud service, Yle a study confirming a Russian satellite deliberately approached a radar satellite of the Finnish firm Iceye, which would not comment, and NOS more Russian arson and explosives in Europe, while Poland signed a $300 million Palantir contract and Canada has not made telecoms remove Huawei equipment. Its case against says nothing names a contractor in the Air Force breach.
threads.direction: It has moved from states spying and sabotaging through private firms told to defend themselves to militaries running parts of their security on firms' clouds and satellites, with disclosure left to the firms.

threads.label: Blockades, and Washington choosing who sells oil
threads.text: Begun on 27 November, marked plausible: Iranian drones were reported killing two Italian technicians in Kuwait, which Iran denies, the Houthis struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, Iraq closed its crossings with Iran and Syria against oil smuggling, Hamas said Gaza's blockade continues and Russia and Poland argued over a Baltic blockade, joined as truces leaving blockades in place. On 28 November it was carried on, marked plausible: US forces disabled a commercial ship trying to leave Iran and Tehran vowed to confront the blockade, Reuters reported Washington urging Iraq and Venezuela to leave OPEC, Trump backed Iraq's smuggling crackdown, Iraq restarted its pipeline to Turkey at 300,000 barrels a day and Lukoil agreed to sell its foreign assets. Gaza and the Baltic dropped out. Its case against says the OPEC report is one unconfirmed Reuters account and Lukoil's sale follows Ukraine sanctions.
threads.direction: It has moved from blockades left in place by truces in the Gulf, Gaza and the Baltic to a US blockade of Iran read as one part of Washington deciding which producers sell oil and by which route.

threads.label: Deaths in fires and blasts paid by donors
threads.text: Begun on 27 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept since 22 November, so the story is older than its first narrative. The Al-Warraq fuel tanker fire in Cairo killed 31, a candy factory fire in Indonesia killed 26, a building collapsed in Karachi and an explosion hit Lanús near Buenos Aires. Payment has come from a Saudi official's EGP 43 million, an Egyptian ministry account for business donors, an airline paying a bride after a newspaper story and a charity festival in Lanús, with Indonesia's state social insurer the exception; Sindh suspended its building control chief rather than naming an owner. The join is that where liability cover is thin, deaths are paid for by gift or the state. Its case against says donations are reported and insurance payouts are not. No narrative carried it on 28 November.

threads.label: Degrees and records deciding who may run
threads.text: Begun on 27 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept since 19 November, so the story is older than its first narrative. Colombia's National University denied that congresswoman Luz Verónica Estrada graduated, prosecutors suspended her and two more Historic Pact lawmakers face questions; on 26 November a Turkish court upheld the stripping of Ekrem İmamoğlu's degree, ending his chance to run for president; Indonesia withholds two vice-presidential contenders' health results, Tinubu's records are disputed and Peru's electoral board halted López Aliaga. The join is that the body issuing or judging a required document holds a veto on candidacy. Its case against says Colombia requires no degree for Congress and the cases may share only paper. Gibran's resignation over a certificate on 12 November sits in the leaders' children thread. No narrative carried it on 28 November.

threads.label: Governments securing their own fuel as climate talks fail
threads.text: Begun on 10 November with a narrative the Chronicle had not given a thread: as the last four years were confirmed the hottest, governments sought new gas and LNG while the climate summit planned electrification. After fifteen editions without a narrative it was resumed on 28 November, marked plausible: the BBC and RNZ reported the climate talks' collapse and Handelsblatt global temperature above two degrees for a week, while Australia's parliament passed a domestic gas reservation scheme, Argentine firms and provinces sought to slow old oilfield decline, Colombia's tax law was forecast to raise electric car prices by 14% and Indonesia answered the OECD on its energy subsidies. The join is each government putting its own fuel and budget first. Its case against says none was decided in response to the summit. COP31's failure on 22 November sits in the consensus forums thread.
threads.direction: It has moved from governments seeking gas while the summit planned electrification to governments reserving their own supply after the talks failed, with the cost of switching left to buyers and donors.

threads.label: Old diseases returning where routine control stopped
threads.text: Begun on 28 November with a narrative marked plausible, built from a subject the site's notebook had kept for some days before any narrative, so the story is older than its first narrative; its claim counts the fortnight from 17 November. The US and Mexico have been reported losing measles elimination, Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 12,000 cases while UN peacekeepers rescue Ebola teams from fighting in Ituri, Gaza's doctors warn of a meningitis wave, experts urge African governments to fund HIV treatment for 20 million people themselves and Israel recorded its 122nd rabies case of the year; Uganda began Africa's first mRNA vaccine trial against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The join is control that rested on routine work, interrupted by war, withdrawn aid or refusal. Its case against says the diseases share nothing biologically and tuberculosis and cholera are absent from the sample.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

The thread now covers ground the Iran war thread held, so the reason given for keeping them apart no longer holds.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on the editions since 26 October, with none stamped 28 October, 9 November, 15 and 16 November or 23 November, drawn from whichever publishers the collection reads and capped in how many headlines each may supply. Today three of four narratives reach back to earlier ones, two by resuming after gaps, one of fifteen editions, so much of the continuity here is produced by a brief that asks the writer to find it, and the fuel narrative's own case against says none of its events answered the summit. The blockades thread now carries the Iran war's events while the Iran thread is kept silent and apart; that division is my judgment, kept from earlier versions, and merging them would read the past week differently. Its newest turn rests on one Reuters account of US pressure on OPEC members that neither government has confirmed, and the one expectation kept today, Iraq's pipeline to Turkey, turns on disputes between Baghdad, Erbil and Ankara as much as on Hormuz. The diseases thread may be joined only by the season and by which outbreaks get covered, and the spying thread's newest narrative is marked tentative with no contractor named in the Air Force breach and 1Password tied to no military.
line: On 28 November 2026 US forces disabled a ship trying to leave Iran under blockade, and Iraq restarted its oil pipeline to Turkey at 300,000 barrels a day.
revision: Two threads were begun: one on old diseases returning, built from the notebook, and one on governments securing their own fuel, which takes up the unthreaded 10 November gas narrative; the spying thread was revived after two editions. The trade deals and civilian places threads fell silent, the blockades thread's label and direction were rewritten and its reason for standing apart from the Iran thread withdrawn, and the standing was rewritten.
